facts.statement: Foraminacephale was a pachycephalosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous Campanian stage in Canada.
facts.quote: Foraminacephale (meaning "foramina head") is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from Late Cretaceous (Campanian stage) deposits of Canada.

facts.statement: Foraminacephale lived approximately 77 to 73 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 77-73 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Foraminacephale was a small, bipedal herbivore characterized by a thickened dome on its skull.
facts.quote: Foraminacephale, as a pachycephalosaurid, was a small, bipedal herbivore with a thickened dome on its skull.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Foraminacephale at 1.5 meters and its weight at 10 kilograms in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 1.5 m, its weight at 10 kg.

facts.statement: The top surface of the Foraminacephale skull dome is punctuated by many small pits known as foramina.
facts.quote: In Foraminacephale, the top surface of the dome is punctuated by many small pits, the eponymous foramina

facts.statement: The squamosal bone forms a tall, mostly smooth bar underneath the dome, featuring six nodes along the bottom edge and one additional corner node.
facts.quote: The squamosal bone forms a tall bar of completely smooth bone underneath the dome, save for six bony nodes that line the bottom edge of the dome and an additional "corner" node just below.

facts.statement: Foraminacephale is distinguished by prominent grooves between the central and lateral lobes of the dome and a slit-like opening of the temporal bone.
facts.quote: there are prominent grooves between the central lobe and the lateral lobes, and the opening of the temporal bone is slit-like.

facts.statement: The holotype of Foraminacephale is specimen CMN 1423, a nearly complete skull dome collected in Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta, in 1902.
facts.quote: The holotype of Foraminacephale is CMN 1423, a nearly complete frontoparietal dome collected in Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta in 1902 and reported on during the same year.

facts.statement: The fossil layers containing Foraminacephale belong to the Dinosaur Park Formation of the Belly River Group.
facts.quote: The layers of rock where the specimen were found belong to the Dinosaur Park Formation of the Belly River Group.

facts.statement: Lawrence Lambe first assigned the holotype specimen to a new species of Stegoceras in 1918.
facts.quote: CMN 1423 was first assigned to a new species of Stegoceras by Lawrence Lambe in 1918

facts.statement: The specimen was later reassigned to the genus Prenocephale in 2000 and then to Sphaerotholus in 2010.
facts.quote: Later, it was assigned to Prenocephale by Robert M. Sullivan in 2000, and then it was assigned to Sphaerotholus by Longrich, Sankey & Tanke in 2010.

facts.statement: A 2016 phylogenetic analysis placed Foraminacephale within the Pachycephalosaurinae, more derived than Stegoceras but more basal than Prenocephale.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis in 2016 found that Foraminacephale was a member of the Pachycephalosaurinae, in a more derived position than Stegoceras, but in a more basal position than Prenocephale.

facts.statement: Micro-CT scans of a potential Foraminacephale specimen support the hypothesis that pachycephalosaurids likely engaged in head-butting behavior.
facts.quote: Micro-CT scans of a potential specimen, identified as cf. Foraminacephale brevis, support that pachycephalosaurids likely engaged in head-butting.

facts.statement: Histological analysis showed that Foraminacephale domes became less porous with age, ranging from 1.67% empty space in juveniles to 0.25% in adults.
facts.quote: Histology of the specimens showed that the domes became less porous with age - the smallest specimen's skull was 1.67% empty space, while the largest specimen's skull was 0.25% empty space.

facts.statement: The supratemporal fenestrae in Foraminacephale are slit-like and seal shut very early in development, unlike the round openings that remain open longer in Stegoceras.
facts.quote: The supratemporal fenestrae on the top of the skulls of Foraminacephale are slit-like, as opposed to Stegoceras where they are round, and they seal shut very early in ontogeny as opposed to remaining open more-or-less throughout the animal's lifespan.

facts.statement: There was considerable debate over whether Stegoceras brevis represented a distinct species or merely a sexual morph of S. validum.
facts.quote: there was considerable debate over whether "S." brevis represented a truly distinct animal or simply a morph, perhaps the female, of S. validum.

facts.statement: Due to a lack of understanding of pachycephalosaur growth, researchers have debated whether material from the Belly River Group represents a single species or four different genera.
facts.quote: Because of a lack of understanding of pachycephalosaur ontogeny, various authors have assigned this material to anywhere from a single species, Stegoceras validum, to four different genera.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen CMN 1423 is an almost complete frontoparietal dome collected from the Provincial Dinosaur Park in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de Foraminacephale es CMN 1423, un domo frontoparietal casi completo recolectado en el Parque Provincial de los Dinosaurios, en Alberta, Canadá.

facts.statement: Various other fragments representing juveniles, subadults, and adults have been found in that geological formation.
facts.quote: Varios otros fragmentos del animal se han hallado en esas formación geológica, que representan individuos juveniles, subadultos y adultos.

facts.statement: A specimen from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation previously assigned to Foraminacephale, CMN 11316, was reidentified as an indeterminate juvenile pachycephalosaur.
facts.quote: Otro espécimen de la formación Cañón Horseshoe antes asignado a Foraminacephale, CMN 11316, fue reidentificado como un paquicefalosaurino juvenil indeterminado.

facts.statement: Lawrence Lambe originally assigned CMN 1423 to a new species of Stegoceras in 1918.
facts.quote: CMN 1423 fue asignado originalmente a una nueva especie de Stegoceras por Lawrence Lambe en 1918

facts.statement: The specimen was later assigned to Prenocephale by Robert M. Sullivan.
facts.quote: Posteriormente, fue asignado a Prenocephale por Robert M. Sullivan.

facts.statement: In 2011, Ryan Schott proposed the new genus name Foraminacephale in his master's thesis, resulting in the new combination Foraminacephale brevis.
facts.quote: En 2011, Ryan Schott sugirió un nuevo nombre de género, Foraminacephale, en su tesis de maestría en ciencias, resultando en la nueva combinación Foraminacephale brevis.

facts.statement: Schott and David Evans formally renamed "S." brevis as Foraminacephale brevis in 2016.
facts.quote: Schott y David Evans renombraron formalmente a "S." brevis como Foraminacephale brevis en 2016.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Latin word foramina, meaning "holes", with cephale, the Greek-derived form for "head", referring to the multiple perforations covering the top of the dome.
facts.quote: el nombre del género combina la palabra en latín foramina, "forámenes", con cephale, la forma latinizada del griego para "cabeza", en referencia a las múltiples perforaciones que cubrían la cima del domo.

facts.statement: A 2016 phylogenetic analysis found Foraminacephale to be a member of the subfamily Pachycephalosaurinae, in a position more derived than Stegoceras but more basal than Prenocephale.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético publicado en 2016 encontró que Foraminacephale era un miembro de la subfamilia Pachycephalosaurinae, en una posición más derivada que Stegoceras, pero más basal con respecto a Prenocephale.

facts.statement: The parent group of Foraminacephale is Pachycephalosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Pachycephalosaurinae

facts.statement: Foraminacephale belongs to the family Pachycephalosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Pachycephalosauridae

facts.statement: Foraminacephale is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Foraminacephale lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Measurements of 27 different points on 21 Foraminacephale skulls showed that the dome became proportionally taller with age but did not widen significantly.
facts.quote: Las mediciones de 27 puntos diferentes en 21 cráneos de Foraminacephale mostraron que el domo se volvía proporcionalmente más alto con la edad, pero no se ensanchaba de forma significativa.

facts.statement: Histology showed that domes became less porous with age; the smallest specimen's skull had 1.67% empty space, while the largest had 0.25%.
facts.quote: La histología de los especímenes mostró que los domos se hacían menos porosos con la edad, en el cráneo del espécimen más pequeño tenía un 1.67% de espacio vacío, mientras que en el del de mayor tamaño el espacio vacío corresponde al 0.25%.

facts.statement: Generally, the frontal zone of the dome was more porous than the parietal zone.
facts.quote: En general, la zona frontal del domo era más porosa que la parietal.

facts.statement: Unlike young Stegoceras which have a flat dome, even the smallest Foraminacephale specimens have a slightly domed parietal.
facts.quote: En los Stegoceras jóvenes, el domo es plano, sin embargo, incluso en los menores especímenes de Foraminacephale, el parietal ya está levemente abovedado.

facts.statement: The supratemporal fenestrae in Foraminacephale skulls are slit-shaped, unlike the rounded ones in Stegoceras, and sealed earlier in ontogenetic development rather than remaining visible throughout life.
facts.quote: Las fenestras supratemporales en la zona superior de los cráneos de Foraminacephale son en forma de rendija, a diferencia de Stegoceras en el que estas eran redondeadas, y se sellaban más tempranamente en el desarrollo ontogénico en lugar de permanecer más o menos visibles durante la vida del animal.

facts.statement: In Foraminacephale, the squamosal and postorbital bones became part of the dome much faster, the dome thickened at a slower rate, and the sides were less angular than in Stegoceras.
facts.quote: Más aún, en Foraminacephale, los huesos escamoso y postorbital se volvían parte del domo mucho más rápidamente, el domo se engrosaba a una tasa más lenta, y los lados del domo eran menos angulosos que en Stegoceras.

facts.statement: The 2016 description of Foraminacephale recognized four different pachycephalosaur taxa from the Belly River Group: Stegoceras, Foraminacephale, Hanssuesia, and Colepiocephale, though specimens referred to Hanssuesia likely represent more than one known species.
facts.quote: La descripción de 2016 de Foraminacephale reconoció a cuatro taxones diferentes de paquicefalosaurios del Grupo Belly River: Stegoceras, Foraminacephale, Hanssuesia y Colepiocephale, aunque los especímenes que han sido referidos a Hanssuesia probablemente representan a más de una de las especies conocidas.

facts.statement: There was considerable debate over whether "S." brevis represented a distinct animal or was simply a morph, perhaps the female, of S. validum.
facts.quote: desde entonces hubo un considerable debate sobre si "S." brevis representaba realmente a un animal distinto o era simplemente un morfo, quizás la hembra, de S. validum.

facts.statement: The topology of this phylogenetic tree is not very stable, probably due to the incompleteness of many pachycephalosaur specimens.
facts.quote: La topología de este árbol filogenético no es muy estable, probablemente debido a lo incompleto de muchos especímenes de paquicefalosáuridos.
